title: Self-reference: the diagonal lemma and undefinability of truth

based_on.title: An Introduction to Gödel's Theorems, second edition, corrected Logic Matters reprint

summary: Construct sentences that describe their own codes, and prove that no arithmetic formula defines truth for all arithmetic sentences.
abstract: A sentence of arithmetic can describe a number, and that number can be the code of the sentence itself. We construct this kind of self-reference using the substitution operation already available on formula codes. The diagonal lemma says that any arithmetic property of a code has a sentence that is provably equivalent to that property of its own code. Applying the construction to a proposed truth predicate yields Tarski's theorem: no arithmetic formula captures truth for every arithmetic sentence. We distinguish this limit on definability from a limit on what a consistent theory can prove, and explain why fixing numerical parameters does not remove it.
